resources.string: Currently %1$s - Move keyboard cycles through these

Center is one full-width keyboard. Dual puts two full copies side by side. Split cuts the key grid in half and duplicates the middle column when the column count is odd (on S12, only the center column is duplicated). Left and Right stay hidden here until they park a narrower keyboard.
On - Dual is skipped when two copies would make keys narrower than %1$d dp
Off - Dual is used even when keys would be squeezed
On a phone in portrait, two full copies of a 5-column layout become too skinny to type on. Turn this off if you still want Dual on a narrow screen.
On - Split is skipped when the screen is taller than it is wide
Off - Split is used whenever it is enabled

Split parks two halves on the left and right. In portrait there is no room between them, so Move keyboard skips Split. Landscape keeps it. Dual has its own cramped check. Turn this off to cycle Split in portrait too.
On - a notice names the layout or position after you switch
Off - switching layout or position stays silent
A brief notice on the keyboard names the layout after Switch language, or the position after Move keyboard.
On - a notice confirms after a successful copy

A brief notice on the keyboard appears only after copy succeeds. With Use private clipboard on, a muted \"private\" label sits beside Copy. Editors that handle copy themselves, such as some terminals, do not show it.
On - a notice confirms after a successful cut

A brief notice on the keyboard appears only after cut succeeds. With Use private clipboard on, a muted \"private\" label sits beside Cut. Editors that handle cut themselves, such as some terminals, do not show it.

On - Bitwarden and other Autofill services can show chips above the keyboard
Off - Autofill stays in the system dropdown instead of this keyboard

This uses Android Autofill. Any Autofill service you pick in system settings can show chips above the keyboard if it supports inline suggestions - for example Bitwarden, Google Password Manager, or 1Password. The app you are typing into must expose Autofill on its login fields; otherwise no chips appear. Chrome also needs Autofill using another service.

Tap a chip to fill. Swipe right on space fills the top (non-logo) chip. The keyboard never sees the password.

## Bitwarden

Set Bitwarden as the Autofill service in system settings. In Bitwarden, set Display autofill suggestions to Inline (not Popup). Popup and keyboard chips are mutually exclusive there.

## Debug

af=y [6] means this field has Autofill and 6 chips are on the keyboard. Brackets are wait / 0 / N / fail / - (Android asked / no chips / chip count / inflate failed / idle). af=n means no Autofill id. af=off / af=na is Inline off / below Android 11.

The hide key on the keyboard writes the same Appearance switches as the hide-letter rows. It only changes the groups you select here. Groups you leave unselected stay as they are. If any selected group is visible, the key hides all of them. If they are all already hidden, the key shows them again.

On - repeated space taps cycle space, comma, period, question, exclamation, colon, semicolon
Off - each space tap only inserts a space

Within one second, and only if the cursor has not moved, each further tap replaces the previous ending (space -> \", \" -> \". \" -> \"? \" -> \"! \" -> \": \" -> \"; \", then wraps). Sliding on space does not advance the cycle. Holding space to repeat only inserts spaces.

Access hidden symbol keys without switching to numeric view
Slide and hold to repeat cursor movement, slide-return-hold for word movement. Backspace: slide-hold to repeat delete, slide-return-hold for word delete.
On - a quick tap queues Esc as a Meta-via-Escape combo for the next key; tapping Esc again while queued sends a real Escape instead
Off - Esc always just sends a real Escape, with no combo behavior

\"Meta via Escape\" is a standard terminal convention (Emacs and most terminals treat \"Esc x\" as \"M-x\"), which is what lets Esc double as a modifier here. Holding Esc while typing other keys sends that combo for as long as it\'s held; a quick tap queues it for just the next key. Tapping Esc again while it\'s still queued (Esc+Esc) sends a plain Escape instead of silently clearing the queue - the escape hatch for when you actually just wanted to press Escape.
On - a quick tap queues Ctrl for the next key; hold keeps it active across several keys
Off - Ctrl always just sends a Ctrl key event, with no combo behavior

When on, tap is one-shot (C-x) and hold stays active while the key is down (C-x then C-s without re-tapping Ctrl). When off, this key always sends the actual Ctrl key, like any other command, including repeat-on-hold.
On - a quick tap queues Alt for the next key; hold keeps it active across several keys
Off - Alt always just sends an Alt key event, with no combo behavior
Same activation shape as Ctrl: tap is one-shot, hold stays active while down. When off, this key always sends the actual Alt key.
On - a quick tap capitalizes the next character; hold is caps lock until tapped off
Off - Shift always just sends a Shift key event, with no combo behavior
When on, tap is one-shot capitalization and a genuine hold locks caps until Shift is tapped again. When off, this key always sends the actual Shift key.

Off - the keyboard leaves room for the bottom system inset
On - the keyboard never takes over the full screen, even in landscape

Some apps ask the keyboard to take over the whole screen (usually in landscape) so there\'s room to type, hiding the app\'s own content until you\'re done. Turning this on keeps the normal keyboard layout visible instead, at the cost of less room to see what you\'re typing into.

On - Suave Copy/Cut stay inside this keyboard and never write the system clipboard
Off - Copy/Cut use the normal system clipboard, shared with every app

The system clipboard is shared across every app on the device, and some apps or accessibility services can read it. With this on, Suave\'s Copy and Cut keys skip the system clipboard entirely: text is kept for paste inside this keyboard (and stored in history only if history is enabled). You will not be able to paste those copies into another keyboard or clipboard manager.
On - copies from other apps are stored in Suave\'s history
Off - only copies made from this keyboard are stored

Suave cannot read Samsung\'s existing clipboard panel. While this is on and Suave is the keyboard, new system copies are recorded into Suave\'s own list. Swipe left on the 123 or ABC key to open it. The current system clip is also shown there even before it is stored.
On - system clipboard images appear in the clipboard layer and can be stored in history
Off - images are ignored; only text is shown and stored

When on, copying an image while Suave is the keyboard shows it in the clipboard layer for pasting into fields that accept images, and stores it in history if system capture is enabled. Turn off to skip image clips entirely.

The install time is read from the APK at runtime so you can confirm a fresh install actually took effect. The rest names the app currently focused and how its text field was classified.

When **Spacebar multi-taps** is on in Behavior, tapping space again within about one second replaces the previous ending with the next entry here.

The first tap is always a plain space. These entries are only the replacements after that. The engine default cycle is:

`, ` -> `. ` -> `? ` -> `! ` -> `: ` -> `; `

Add your own strings, or tap **Use engine default** to clear a custom list. Sliding or holding space does not advance the cycle.

A typical button has width 1. Important buttons are usually wider, like Return or Space having a width of 2.

Pick which Appearance palette this key uses when letter and control backgrounds are split.

- **Auto** - letter background if the center types text, otherwise control (commands, modifiers, space).
- **Letter** - always the letter background.
- **Control** - always the control background (space, Enter, Shift, and similar).

Adds continuous slide gestures on this key - the Space / Backspace kind of sliding, not a swipe to a zone.

On a letter like A, leave this at **None**. Tap still types the letter; swipes still hit zones. Enabling slide does not change what the key types - it only adds caret or selection sliding on top.

- **None** - taps and swipes only (default for letters).
- **Move cursor** - sliding moves the caret (Space). Holding Shift while sliding extends a selection instead.
- **Select and delete** - sliding extends a selection, then release deletes it (Backspace).

When slide is enabled, **Slide direction** below chooses which way the steps go.

Which way a sustained slide on this key counts steps (only used when Slide behavior is not None).

- **HORIZONTAL** - left / right (typical for Backspace).
- **VERTICAL** - up / down.
- **BOTH** - after you move far enough, the stronger axis (typical for Space).

A short flick can still lock a swipe zone; a sustained move along this direction becomes repeated slide steps.
